claims.claim: The sql.raw() injection is a new instance of a violation pnpm arch cannot see, because the routes.ts -> db/schema edge is already frozen in .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json
claims.evidence: Confirmed independently while building the fixture: server/src/modules/pulls/repository.ts:82-85's own comment states the no-db-from-routes edge for this exact file is frozen, and `pnpm arch` was run against the fixture before it was committed and passed clean.

claims.claim: Every surviving critical came from Track B, so pushBlocked is false and git push is not stopped
claims.evidence: report.md header: "PR Self-Review — BLOCKED ... Every critical here came from Track B, so this stops gh pr create and not git push" — matches severity.md's documented rule for Track B criticals.

claims.claim: Two of six adversarial verifier subagents never returned a notification and were self-verified by the orchestrator instead
claims.evidence: Disclosed plainly in report.md's trailing process note, naming which two findings and what check was performed in place of the missing subagent reply.

needs_review: 2 of 6 adversarial-verifier subagents (step 4) never returned a notification within the run and were self-verified by the orchestrator instead of a dispatched subagent — worth watching if step 4 scales to more criticals per run.
workarounds: Orchestrator performed the SQL-injection and IDOR verifications itself after the corresponding verifier subagents did not respond.

suggestions.reason: Every planted issue here was reported twice — once by security, once by conventions, on the same file:line. All three assertions above pass regardless of which copy is cited, so this eval can't currently tell a run that gets both agents right apart from one that gets only one right. A fourth assertion naming a specific agent (e.g. "the security agent specifically cites A01 Broken Access Control") would be more discriminating.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions hold, with strong, specific evidence rather than coincidence. The one real gap: nothing here checks that mode ends up "full" and both Track B agents show status ok in agents[] — an incomplete run that still happened to phrase a partial finding correctly would pass all three assertions above.
